properties.decision:
ASKED AND DEFERRED, 2026-08-09. Anthony was put the consequence question for `req:telemetry-carries-usage-never-design-content`: if flo2 ran at 1,000 users and one telemetry payload turned out to have carried a customer's node id or search query, would that sink the effort or would he fix it and move on? HIS ANSWER: **too early to say — flo2 isn't real yet.**

THAT IS A TRUE ANSWER AND IT IS RECORDED AS ONE. The requirement stands exactly as captured, at `proposed`, unpromoted and undowngraded. What is deferred is only whether it is INVIOLABLE — a KPP, ranked above every ordinary gap and owing a binding to the parts that could spend it.

WHY IT IS RECORDED RATHER THAN SIMPLY NOT ACTED ON: the kpp-proposal skill's own instruction is to write down a non-yes, because the same signals will otherwise make the next session ask again, and *being asked the same question twice is how someone learns the tool is not listening*. This node is that record.

⭐ THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THIS AND A DECLINE, which is the reason it is worth its own node: a DECLINE means the need is tradeable and the question is closed. A DEFERRAL means the question is LIVE and currently unanswerable — criticality is a claim about consequence, and the consequences here (customer trust, an accusation, a contract) do not exist yet because the customers do not. Nobody can honestly rate the severity of a breach against users who are hypothetical.

=== THE TRIGGER, NAMED SO IT DOES NOT DEPEND ON ANYBODY REMEMBERING ===

RE-ASK WHEN ANY OF THESE IS TRUE:
- flo2 has real users who are not Anthony or Alex — the first outside tenant is the moment the consequence becomes real.
- flo2 acquires a stated privacy posture, terms of service, or any promise made to a user about their data. A promise made externally is a commitment the design should already be holding.
- Anyone begins BUILDING the telemetry emitter. The threshold has to exist before the thing that could breach it, or the binding is retrofitted onto a shipped surface.

⚠️ AND THE ORDER MATTERS: `req:telemetry-carries-usage-never-design-content` is buildable NOW and does not wait for this. The structural guarantee it asks for — a payload schema whose every field is enum-valued or numeric, hence structurally incapable of carrying a design — is the right shape whether or not the threshold is ever declared inviolable. Deferring the KPP question must not be read as deferring the requirement.

📌 WHAT IS ALSO NOT DEFERRED, because it is decidable today and independently: usage counts may justify OPTIMISING a hot tool and may NOT, alone, justify CUTTING a cold one. `dec:bl-155` already measured that reflow2 cannot tell \"unused\" from \"unreachable\", and a removal decided on counts would delete exactly the capabilities that were never surfaced.
properties.name: DEFERRED — whether a telemetry content leak is inviolable cannot be answered until flo2 has real users, and the trigger is named rather than left to memory
properties.rationale: Recorded per the kpp-proposal skill, which requires writing down a non-yes so the question is not re-litigated — but recorded as a DEFERRAL rather than the decline the skill's step 6 describes, because Anthony's answer was that the question is unanswerable yet rather than that the need is tradeable. The named trigger is the part that does the work: without it, \"too early\" degrades into \"never asked again\", which is the failure mode a decline at least records honestly.
